## 2. Comprehensive Concept Deep-Dive & Source PYQ Links

### 2.1 Ionization Enthalpy & Electron Gain Enthalpy (Periodic Trends)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **133 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Periodic variations of ionization energy, exceptions due to half-filled/fully-filled subshells ($\text{N} > \text{O}, \text{Be} > \text{B}$), and electron gain enthalpy.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
Z_{\text{eff}} = Z - \sigma, \quad \Delta_{\text{eg}}H(\text{Cl}) < \Delta_{\text{eg}}H(\text{F}) \text{ (Cl is most negative in periodic table)}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Ionization enthalpy of Nitrogen is HIGHER than Oxygen due to stable half-filled $2p^3$ subshell ($\text{N}: 2s^2 2p^3 > \text{O}: 2s^2 2p^4$).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Chlorine has MORE negative electron gain enthalpy than Fluorine because of compact size and high inter-electronic repulsion in $2p$ of Fluorine.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"$\text{Match List - I with List - II.}$ List - I Electronic configuration of neutral atom (where $n=2$ ) List - II $1^{\text{st}}$ Ionizatio..."* — **Correct Answer: A**
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"The $1^{\text{st}}$ ionization enthalpy for Mg is $+737kJ/mol$ . The most probable estimated value of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ ionization enthalp..."* — **Correct Answer: C**
- **[2026 Morning Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"In period 4 of the periodic table, the elements with highest and lowest atomic radii are respectively...."* — **Correct Answer: C**
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of ' X ' and phosphorus is higher than that of the ..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Atomic & Ionic Radii Trends (Radii)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **47 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Covalent, van der Waals, and ionic radii trends across periods and groups, and size shrinkage in isoelectronic ions.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{For isoelectronic: } r \propto \frac{1}{Z} \implies \text{N}^{3-} > \text{O}^{2-} > \text{F}^- > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Al}^{3+}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Noble gas radii are measured as van der Waals radii, making them appear abnormally larger than adjacent halogens.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Due to lanthanoid contraction (poor shielding of $4f$ electrons), $4d$ and $5d$ transition elements have nearly identical radii (e.g. $\text{Zr} \approx \text{Hf}$).

synthesis.traps_and_pitfalls:
## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Periodic Table & Periodicity

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
